name: Battery status
plain: Reads charge level and charging state where the browser still offers it.
meaning: Level and times (level, charging, chargingTime, dischargingTime) once enabled short term tracking across sites. Firefox removed it; Chrome limits it to secure contexts.

limits.headline: Can see your battery level and charging state in Chrome and Edge
limits.user_action: Nothing. No pop up is shown
can: Check your charge level and whether you are plugged in
See time left to full or to empty
Switch to a low power mode when your battery is low
Use level and charge time together as a short term tracking clue
cannot: Work in Safari or on iPhone
Work in Firefox, which removed it
Work on pages that are not HTTPS
See battery health or exact power draw
limits.reach_label: Current battery, while the page is open
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, and Samsung Internet allow it. Firefox removed it and Safari never offered it.

story.what_it_is: Reads how full your battery is and whether you are plugged in, where the browser still allows it.

marketing.name: Battery Status API
marketing.pitch: Describes how a page reads charge level and charging state where browsers support it.

story.for_you: You never see it asked. If it helps, a web app might lower its animations when you are low on power. If it does not, a site could quietly note that your battery is at 43 percent and charging.
story.for_makers: Web apps use it to save power on phones and laptops. Trackers once used it as a short-lived ID, because level and charge time are the same across sites for a few minutes. That is why Firefox and Safari removed it and Chrome limits it.

use_cases.example: A web game drops from 60 to 30 frames a second when the phone is under 15 percent and not charging.
A streaming site starts at a lower resolution on a laptop that is unplugged and nearly flat.
A browser notes app forces an immediate save when it sees the battery is almost out.
A web map in navigation mode shows a plug-in reminder when the phone is low on charge.
A fingerprinting script uses level and charge time as a short-term ID to link two visits in the same hour.
Researchers warned that a shop could change a price for a person who looks desperate for power; this is a risk, not a known practice.
